body: 13 Nov 2026 night, WHERE MATCHING LIVES (read-only note for the advisor's ruling; N-23 stays parked until it is made). Facts, read in the code: (1) The server has NO search endpoint (server/encore_server/encore_server/api.py); the only text matching on the server is textnorm.py (norm_artist, norm_title) used by the cover finder, refs and the keeper, and it folds to ASCII (audit B-37). (2) The phone searches its own library with a local FTS5 index (app/lib/data/db/app_database.dart: track_fts, album_fts, artist_fts, tokenizer unicode61 remove_diacritics 2, prefix 2 and 3) through search_dao.dart, offline and instant; its other matcher is domain/text_match.dart (keeps every script) plus domain/search_rank.dart (scores). (3) The catalogue half of a search is Deezer, asked by the PHONE today (a debt against ADR-R38, goal zero: P2-12 moves it to the server); Deezer does its own fuzzy matching. (4) Audit B-46 / the plan: 'One matcher on the server (P2-25); the phone stops matching, or keeps its own only for what is on the phone.' So ADR-R42's rule is already read as: the phone may keep a matcher ONLY for what is on the phone. PROPOSED RULING: split N-23. N-23a (phone, offline, now): typo tolerance for the library part, inside the local search the phone already owns: candidates from the existing FTS index by prefix/trigram of the typed words, then ranked by edit distance in search_rank.dart (one letter wrong in a name of 5 or more letters, never for 1 to 3 letters); no second matcher, no server call. N-23b (server, after P2-12): the catalogue part gets its tolerance from Deezer through the server's own search; nothing to build on the phone. Also needed before N-23a: one shared normaliser so text_match.dart, search_dao.dart and textnorm.py stop disagreeing on alphabets (B-46/P2-25), or at least the phone's two (text_match and the FTS tokenizer) agree.
